title: Dragon Essence Forge — Post-Process Alchemy
description: Two dragons face each other on pedestals: the Attenuation Dragon absorbs light while the Dispersion Dragon refracts it. The user manipulates a shared post-processing pipeline of six chained effects, balancing a conservation law where total visual energy across both dragons must remain constant. Adjusting bloom on one dragon steals luminance from the other, requiring careful multi-input coupling, with full undo/redo support.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with the postprocessing ecosystem (import maps from cdn.jsdelivr.net for three, three/addons). Load DragonAttenuation.glb on the left and DragonDispersion.glb on the right, both centered and facing each other on circular stone pedestals, separated by 4 units. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0,2,6) looking at origin with OrbitControls. Add a warm directional light from above-right and a cool fill light from below-left, plus ambient light. Implement an EffectComposer with a shared render pass and six post-process effects applied via ShaderPass or built-in passes: (1) UnrealBloomPass, (2) a custom chromatic aberration shader, (3) a vignette shader, (4) a film grain shader, (5) a color balance/hue-shift shader, (6) a pixelation shader. Create a right-side HTML panel with sliders for each effect's intensity (0-100). Implement an energy conservation law: the sum of all six effect intensities must always equal 300. When the user increases one slider, automatically reduce others proportionally to maintain the sum, visually coupling the effects. Each dragon receives different weighting: the Attenuation dragon is more affected by bloom and vignette, while the Dispersion dragon responds more to chromatic aberration and hue-shift. Achieve this by rendering each dragon in a separate layer and compositing with different effect strengths derived from the slider values and per-dragon weight multipliers. Implement a full undo/redo stack (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z) that records each slider interaction as a state snapshot, displayed as a small history counter in the top-left corner. Add a 'Randomize' button that animates all sliders to new valid positions respecting the conservation constraint. The task requires at least 10 deliberate slider adjustments to reach a target aesthetic shown as a small reference thumbnail in the bottom-right corner (a preset combination). Display a match percentage that compares current effect values to the target. When match exceeds 95%, show a success banner.
